holidays.name: National Beer Day
holidays.description: Americans raise a frosty mug to celebrate the day in 1933 when beer became legal again after Prohibition. Cheers, with a side of pretzels.
holidays.origin: The Cullen-Harrison Act took effect on April 7, 1933, allowing beer with up to 3.2% alcohol by weight to be sold. The modern observance was started by Justin Smith, who created a Facebook page in 2009 and pushed for the day to be recognized.
holidays.funFact: When the law took effect at 12:01 a.m., crowds gathered outside breweries, and trucks of beer were sent to the White House. President Franklin D. Roosevelt reportedly said, 'I think this would be a good time for a beer.'

holidays.name: No Housework Day
holidays.description: A guilt-free holiday encouraging you to put down the mop, ignore the dishes, and let the dust bunnies live in peace for 24 hours.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance was reportedly created as a lighthearted excuse to skip chores. It has no single documented founder and spread through lists of quirky celebrations.
holidays.funFact: The average person spends roughly 2 to 3 hours a day on household chores, so skipping a day gives you back a surprising chunk of time for naps.

holidays.name: World Health Day
holidays.description: A global health awareness day where the world focuses on a different health theme each year, from mental health to universal health coverage.
holidays.origin: It marks the founding of the World Health Organization on April 7, 1948. The first World Health Assembly in 1948 decided to observe it, and it has been celebrated since 1950.
holidays.funFact: The WHO is credited with coordinating the global effort that eradicated smallpox, declared eliminated in 1980, which is the only human disease eradicated so far.

holidays.name: Caramel Popcorn Day
holidays.description: A sweet and crunchy snack holiday devoted to popcorn coated in gooey caramel. Perfect for movie nights and for sticking to your teeth.
holidays.origin: A food-industry style unofficial observance, it grew from the popularity of caramel-coated popcorn, which has been sold since the late 1800s. Cracker Jack, introduced at the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, popularized the treat.
holidays.funFact: Cracker Jack was mentioned in the 1908 song 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game,' making caramel popcorn part of baseball tradition.

holidays.name: Day of Remembrance for Victims of the Rwanda Genocide
holidays.description: Though not a quirky celebration, this serious observance sits alongside the fun ones on April 7 and invites reflection, education, and a commitment to preventing atrocities.
holidays.origin: The United Nations designated April 7 as the International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda. The date marks the start of the 100 days of violence in 1994.
holidays.funFact: Rwanda holds a 100-day commemoration period called Kwibuka, which means 'to remember' in Kinyarwanda.
